sb_prompt: DISCUSS RECENT SOCIAL CHANGES.  HOW IS LIFE IN AMERICA DIFFERENT TODAY COMPARED TO LIVING TEN YEARS AGO?
turns: So, you're the farmer, huh? I'm the plumber. See, ten years ago my dad did this stuff without any permits or safety checks, but now the regulations are so strict it feels like the government is trying to stop us from working. It's frustrating, but sometimes I see why they do it. How about you? Did you find things easier or harder than your dad did?
Honestly, it's been harder to get things done, but mostly because the land has changed more than the rules, and I know a guy who lost his whole farm just trying to switch to organic.
That's so sad, did he try to fight the regulations or was it just the soil?
He wasn't sure where to start, the soil tests were confusing and the cost was just too high, so he basically quit before he even began.

Yeah, that really sucks. I had a neighbor a few years back who wanted to install a new septic system for an old farmhouse, but the permits took six months and the inspector kept changing his mind on what counts as "safe," so he just gave up and sold the place to someone else.
Yeah, that's exactly what happened to my buddy, he just walked away because the paperwork was too much.
Yeah, it's just that much red tape killing the spirit of the job sometimes.
Yeah, it just feels like we're fighting a war we didn't start.
I guess I still get some contracts though, so maybe I'll keep doing it even if it's annoying.
I mean, maybe I'll hang it up too before the paperwork eats me alive.
Yeah, I guess I'll keep doing it, but I'd sure love to hear more about what's actually made things worse for you besides the rules.
Actually, it's not just the rules, it's that the big companies bought up most of the good land, so now I'm stuck farming on dirt that was probably paved over before.
That's a real shame about the land.
Yeah, like right down the road, a huge strip mall used to be a wheat field.
Yeah, that's just crazy, a whole strip mall on dirt that used to grow wheat?
Yeah, they paved over the best soil just to put in those big boxes.
That's wild, I can't even imagine losing that kind of ground.
Yeah, it's just that they don't care about the soil anymore, they just want square footage.
That's really hard to lose, not being able to grow food where you want.
Yeah, they just fill the gaps with parking lots and strip malls, there's barely any space left for us to farm anymore.
Yeah, we're just filling in the cracks where they can't build anything else.
Yeah, it feels like the whole country is just turning into concrete.
Yeah, it's just everywhere you look now.
Yeah, I guess it's just that everywhere you drive, it's all parking lots and nothing left to grow.
Yeah, it's just that everything's just too built up now.
I guess it's just hard to feel like you belong when you can't plant a garden anywhere.
Yeah, it feels like there's nowhere left to put roots down.
Yeah, it feels like the ground is just gone before you even get to plant.
Yeah, it's just that there's nowhere to put roots down.
Yeah, maybe we just gotta learn to fight it from here.
Yeah, maybe we just gotta figure out how to make a life in what's left.
Yeah, maybe we can at least protect what we have left.
Yeah, maybe that's the only way to keep us around.
Yeah, maybe we can at least protect what we have left.
Yeah, that's the only thing left to fight for, I guess.
Yeah, maybe that's the only way to keep us around.
Yeah, I suppose we have to hang on to what's left.
Yeah, I suppose we just have to hold on tight.
